name: Min Aung Hlaing
role: President of Myanmar (inaugurated Apr 10, 2026; elected Apr 3 — 429/584 votes). Completed five-day India state visit (May 30–June 3) — first foreign trip as civilian president; bilateral summit with PM Modi June 1 (trade $1.95B FY2025-26, Kaladan MMTTP, IMCOR/IMNEX defense frameworks, cybercrime). Returned June 3 to Naypyidaw. Will NOT attend ASEAN-Russia Summit in Kazan (June 17–19); FM Than Swe attending in his place — Myanmar is ASEAN-Russia coordinator. Excluded from ASEAN Leaders' Summit in Cebu (May 7, 2026 — only Permanent Secretary attended). Myanmar junta rebuked Timor-Leste President Ramos-Horta (June 6–7) for calling Myanmar 'a stain on ASEAN.' Retired as C-in-C Mar 30; installed loyalist Ye Win Oo as military chief. Reportedly made secret visit to Toungoo area (Bago Region) June 6 — resistance fired 4 rockets at Toungoo Air Base in apparent response. Made first official Thailand visit Aug 6-7, 2026, meeting PM Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok — signed labor MOU, agreed to raise bilateral trade to a $12B target, reopened the Second Thailand-Myanmar Friendship Bridge. Thai civil-society groups protested the visit. On Aug 8, Myanmar's Foreign Ministry (under his government) rejected ASEAN's renewed call to free Aung San Suu Kyi and questioned the need for the ASEAN special envoy role. Made his first official visit to Russia August 17-18, 2026, meeting President Putin in Moscow to discuss the Russia-backed Dawei deep-sea port project alongside energy and nuclear-reactor cooperation; the visit preceded a junta ground offensive to clear land for the Dawei SEZ in Tanintharyi Region.
quote: The military must safeguard the nation's existence. We will work for the country and the people, and hand over power to the winning party after holding a free and fair election.

name: Tin Maung Swe
role: Foreign Minister of Myanmar under SAC civilian government (since April 10, 2026). Completed first official visit to China (June 4–6, 2026) — met Chinese FM Wang Yi in Beijing. Wang Yi pledged to strengthen high-level exchanges, advance CMEC, and jointly combat cross-border cybercrime/scam compounds. Beijing visit follows Wang Yi's Naypyidaw visit (April 25–26) and cemented China's diplomatic endorsement of the new SAC civilian administration. Will represent Myanmar at ASEAN-Russia Summit in Kazan (June 17–19) in Min Aung Hlaing's place.
quote: Myanmar and China share a long history of fraternal friendship. We will work closely together to advance the China-Myanmar Economic Corridor and address shared security challenges.

name: Ye Win Oo
role: Commander-in-Chief, Myanmar Defence Services (installed Mar 31, 2026); longtime intelligence chief and Min Aung Hlaing loyalist; assumed military command following Min Aung Hlaing's retirement to pursue civilian presidency
quote: The Tatmadaw will continue to protect national sovereignty and defend the constitutional order against all threats from terrorist organizations.

name: Soe Win
role: Vice-Senior General; SAC Vice Chairman; now Vice Chairman, State Security & Peace Commission
quote: The military will not allow the country to fall into the hands of terrorists and anarchists who seek to destroy the union.

name: Myat Tun Oo
role: SAC Information Committee Chairman; regime spokesperson; controlled state media propaganda
quote: All military operations target terrorists — not civilians. The claims of human rights organizations are fabrications designed to destabilize Myanmar.

name: Duwa Lashi La
role: NUG Acting President; former Kachin State lawyer and community leader
quote: The SAC junta's brutality will never break the people's will. We will establish a federal democratic union where all citizens have equal rights regardless of ethnicity or religion.

name: Mahn Win Khaing Than
role: NUG Prime Minister; former Lower House Speaker; ethnic Karen NLD leader
quote: This is our darkest moment, but the dawn will come. The people of Myanmar have chosen democracy and will sacrifice everything to achieve it.

name: Aung San Suu Kyi
role: State Counsellor (under house arrest); Nobel Peace Laureate. Sentenced to 27 years by junta courts; sentence nominally reduced to ~22.5 years in Apr 2026 Thingyan amnesty. On Apr 30 / May 1, 2026 — Day 1,918 — Myanmar state media (MRTV) announced her transfer from Naypyidaw Prison to house arrest after 5+ years of near-total isolation. NUG and son Kim Aris rejected the announcement as a 'deceptive political maneuver,' demanded proof of life. Her lawyers were unable to independently verify the transfer. International rights groups called for monitoring access to confirm her condition and welfare. On Aug 3, 2026 she met ICRC Myanmar head of delegation Arnaude de Baecque in Naypyidaw — her first known meeting with a foreign official in years, following mounting international concern about her health; the regime released four photos of the meeting but findings were shared confidentially.
quote: Please take care of yourselves. Do not be reckless. Do not be controlled by fear of the military.

name: Zin Mar Aung
role: NUG Minister for Foreign Affairs; political prisoner under previous junta; international spokesperson
quote: We call on the international community to recognize the NUG as Myanmar's legitimate government and to provide concrete support — not just statements — to the people's struggle for democracy.

name: Twan Mrat Naing (Aung Myo Kyaw)
role: Major General; AA Commander-in-Chief; ULA Chairman; de facto ruler of ~90% of Rakhine State. In a rare May 2026 Diplomat interview, signaled openness to eventual talks with the Myanmar government and addressed the AA's relations with India (Kaladan MMTT Project) and Bangladesh (Rohingya refugee situation). Interview came one week after HRW published its May 18, 2026 report documenting AA's alleged May 2024 Hoyyar Siri Rohingya massacre (170+ killed including 90+ children); AA denies the findings. On Jul 20, 2026, the AA formally rejected Min Aung Hlaing's '100-day peace initiative' invitation, citing continued junta airstrikes on AA territory. Aug 2-6: junta escalated airstrikes and artillery along the Rakhine-Magway border (Nat Yay Kan/Goteseeyoe) to recapture a Chinese gas-pipeline corridor from the AA; AA forces also advanced to within ~2km of Sittwe, the last major Rakhine town in junta hands.
quote: The Arakan Army fights not only to liberate Rakhine but to build a truly federal democratic Myanmar where all peoples can live in dignity and equality. (May 2026: Signaled openness to dialogue with Myanmar government and regional neighbors; denied HRW Rohingya massacre allegations.)

name: Mutu Say Poe
role: KNU (Karen National Union) Chairman; longest-serving ethnic armed organization leader in Myanmar
quote: The Karen people have been fighting for our rights for 70 years. Now we stand with all the peoples of Myanmar to end military dictatorship once and for all.

name: General N'Ban La
role: KIO (Kachin Independence Organisation) Chairman; KIA supreme commander; key NUG ally. KIA announced defensive strategy shift on May 22, 2026 after SAC dispatched 300-vehicle armored convoy to Northern Military Command in Myitkyina — the largest junta reinforcement to Kachin in years. KIA retains all captured positions from April-May 2026 offensive while absorbing SAC's escalatory response. KIA is co-founder of the SCEF resistance coalition (formed March 30, 2026).
quote: The KIA has always defended the Kachin people against military aggression. We will continue to fight until a genuine federal union is established.

name: Lway Yay Mong (Tarng Shawng)
role: TNLA/PSLF Chairman; Three Brotherhood Alliance co-founder; Operation 1027 architect. Issued Apr 15, 2026 statement welcoming Min Aung Hlaing's government. At China-brokered Kunming talks (May 12-13, 2026), rejected junta demand to surrender four northern Shan State towns (Namhkam, Namtu, Mongngawt, Monglon) — showing the limits of Chinese diplomatic leverage over TNLA despite its Apr 15 political reversal.
quote: TNLA Central Executive Committee (Apr 15, 2026): welcomed the formation of the new government by Min Aung Hlaing, expressing hopes for peace and stability in Ta'ang areas. (May 2026: TNLA rejected Chinese-brokered junta demand to surrender four northern Shan towns at Kunming talks.)

name: Peng Daxun
role: MNDAA (Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army) Chairman; Kokang leader; Operation 1027 co-commander
quote: We launched Operation 1027 to restore Kokang's dignity and autonomy, and to liberate northern Shan State from military occupation. We did not expect such a complete victory so quickly.

name: Saw Kyaw Hla / KNDF
role: Karenni Nationalities Defence Force (KNDF) Commander; Kayah State resistance leader
quote: Karenni people have suffered genocidal violence for too long. We fight to defend our homes, our culture, and to build a Karenni State where we live on our own terms.

name: Tom Andrews
role: UN Special Rapporteur on Myanmar Human Rights (2020–2025); called for arms embargo and ICC referral
quote: Myanmar is in a death spiral. The military junta is committing atrocity crimes on a massive scale. The international community must act before it is too late.

name: Wang Yi
role: Chinese Foreign Minister; visited Naypyidaw Apr 25-26, 2026 — met Min Aung Hlaing and FM Tin Maung Swe; pledged to 'firmly support Myanmar in safeguarding its national sovereignty, security and territorial integrity'; agreed to expand bilateral trade (electricity, oil, gas), security cooperation, and joint counter-scam operations; Wang's visit capped a 5-nation Southeast Asia tour and provided China's explicit diplomatic endorsement of the SAC's political transition
quote: China will firmly support Myanmar in safeguarding its national sovereignty, security and territorial integrity. China and Myanmar are bound by ties of 'pauk-phaw' (fraternal) friendship and will work together for the stability and development of both countries.

name: Kyaw Min Htike
role: AAPP (Assistance Association for Political Prisoners) Secretary; documents arrests, torture, and deaths in detention
quote: The junta's prison system is a machine of torture and death. Every day our colleagues are beaten, denied medicine, and disappear into cells from which they never return.

name: Sithu Maung
role: CRPH (Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw) member; NUG ally; activist MP who fled arrest in 2021
quote: We left behind our families, our homes, everything. But we carry with us the mandate of the people who voted for us, and that mandate is to build a democratic Myanmar.

name: Ye Myo Hein
role: PDF Commander-in-Chief; NUG Defense Ministry senior official; leads PDF military coordination
quote: The PDF is not a militia — we are a national defense force fighting for every citizen of Myanmar. Our fighters come from every ethnicity, religion, and region of this country.

name: Tun Khin
role: Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK) President; Rohingya genocide survivor and international advocate
quote: The same military that committed genocide against us now fights for its survival. We Rohingya support democracy but we need guarantees of safety, citizenship rights, and accountability for the 2017 genocide before we can return.

name: ASEAN 5-Point Consensus
role: ASEAN's framework for Myanmar dialogue; largely unimplemented; SAC boycotted multiple summits
quote: ASEAN calls on all parties to exercise utmost restraint and implement the Five Point Consensus. The situation in Myanmar has not improved and represents an ongoing threat to regional stability.

name: SCEF (Steering Council for Federal Democratic Union)
role: Formed March 30, 2026 — Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union; comprises KIO, KNU, CNF (Chin National Front), KNPP (Karenni), NUG, and CRPH; aims to establish transitional federal governance structures for a post-SAC Myanmar. Recognized by IPU (Inter-Parliamentary Union) via CRPH on April 19, 2026. The SCEF represents the most unified formal resistance political coalition since the 2021 coup, bringing together ethnic armed organizations and the parallel civilian government under a shared federal democratic framework. On Aug 5, 2026, following a meeting with Thai and Philippine foreign ministers, SCEF signaled for the first time that it is committed to pursuing negotiations — driven partly by junta battlefield gains in Rakhine/Magway and regional diplomatic pressure. Separately, NUG/PDF commanders from all ten regional commands met Aug 3-6 to plan a shift from 'People's Resistance War' toward a 'Strategic Offensive' phase.
quote: The SCEF is committed to building a federal democratic union that respects the rights of all Myanmar's diverse peoples and replaces the military's illegitimate rule with genuine democratic governance.

name: IPU / CRPH Recognition (Apr 19, 2026)
role: Inter-Parliamentary Union confirmed on April 19, 2026 that it recognizes the Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw (CRPH) as Myanmar's principal parliamentary representative — explicitly rejecting the junta's December 2025 elections and the parliament formed under SAC supervision. The IPU's 180-member body grants CRPH access to inter-parliamentary forums and multilateral observer status.
quote: The IPU reaffirms the CRPH as Myanmar's legitimate parliamentary voice and rejects any process that excludes the democratic will of the Myanmar people. The December 2025 elections held under military control do not meet the basic standards for parliamentary legitimacy.

name: Anutin Charnvirakul
role: Prime Minister of Thailand; hosted Min Aung Hlaing's first official Thailand visit since the 2021 coup (Aug 6-7, 2026) at Government House, Bangkok — signed a labor-cooperation MOU, agreed to raise bilateral trade to a $12B target, and reopened the Second Thailand-Myanmar Friendship Bridge (Mae Sot-Myawaddy). Thailand pledged to work toward Myanmar's 'full reintegration with ASEAN.'
quote: Thailand will work toward Myanmar's full reintegration with ASEAN, while continuing to engage on trade, energy, and border stability that benefit the people of both nations.
